claim: The dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN) is an important source of neuromodulators.
source: The dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN) is an important source of neuromodulators and has been implicated in a wide variety of behavioral and neurological disorders.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract introducing the DRN.

claim: The DRN has been implicated in a wide variety of behavioral and neurological disorders.
source: The dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN) is an important source of neuromodulators and has been implicated in a wide variety of behavioral and neurological disorders.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract, referencing established knowledge about DRN involvement in disorders.

claim: The DRN is subdivided into distinct anatomical subregions comprised of multiple cell types.
source: The DRN is subdivided into distinct anatomical subregions comprised of multiple cell types, and its complex cellular organization has impeded efforts to investigate the distinct circuit and behavioral functions of its subdomains.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract describing the anatomical organization of the DRN.

claim: The complex cellular organization of the DRN has impeded efforts to investigate the distinct circuit and behavioral functions of its subdomains.
source: The DRN is subdivided into distinct anatomical subregions comprised of multiple cell types, and its complex cellular organization has impeded efforts to investigate the distinct circuit and behavioral functions of its subdomains.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract explaining a challenge in DRN research.

claim: The study used single-cell RNA sequencing to map the transcriptional profiles of cells from the mouse DRN.
source: Here we used single-cell RNA sequencing, in situ hybridization, anatomical tracing, and spatial correlation analysis to map the transcriptional and spatial profiles of cells from the mouse DRN.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract describing the methods used.

claim: The analysis of 39,411 single-cell transcriptomes revealed at least 18 distinct neuron subtypes.
source: Our analysis of 39,411 single-cell transcriptomes revealed at least 18 distinct neuron subtypes and 5 serotonergic neuron subtypes with distinct molecular and anatomical properties, including a serotonergic neuron subtype that preferentially innervates the basal ganglia.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract reporting the number of cells analyzed and neuron subtypes identified.

claim: The analysis of 39,411 single-cell transcriptomes revealed 5 serotonergic neuron subtypes with distinct molecular and anatomical properties.
source: Our analysis of 39,411 single-cell transcriptomes revealed at least 18 distinct neuron subtypes and 5 serotonergic neuron subtypes with distinct molecular and anatomical properties, including a serotonergic neuron subtype that preferentially innervates the basal ganglia.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract reporting the number of serotonergic neuron subtypes identified.

claim: A serotonergic neuron subtype preferentially innervates the basal ganglia.
source: Our analysis of 39,411 single-cell transcriptomes revealed at least 18 distinct neuron subtypes and 5 serotonergic neuron subtypes with distinct molecular and anatomical properties, including a serotonergic neuron subtype that preferentially innervates the basal ganglia.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract reporting a finding about a specific serotonergic neuron subtype.

claim: The DRN is the largest of the serotonergic nuclei, containing approximately a third of all serotonergic neurons in the brain.
source: The dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN) is a major source of neuromodulators in the central nervous system, and is the largest of the serotonergic nuclei, containing approximately a third of all serotonergic neurons (5-HT neurons) in the brain (Hornung, 2010).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction citing Hornung, 2010.

claim: DRN 5-HT neurons send highly divergent projections that target many functionally distinct brain regions.

evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction citing multiple sources.

claim: Diverse and at times conflicting functions have been proposed for DRN 5-HT neurons, including arousal.
source: Concordantly, diverse and at times conflicting functions have been proposed for DRN 5-HT neurons, including arousal (Monti, 2010), motor facilitation (Jacobs and Fornal, 1997), behavioral inhibition (Miyazaki et al., 2012), cognitive flexibility (Matias et al., 2017), value representation (Bromberg-Martin et al., 2010; Cohen et al., 2015; Hayashi et al., 2015; Li et al., 2016), motor learning (Kawashima et al., 2016), mood (Cools et al., 2008), and regulation of social interactions (Dölen et al., 2013; Niederkofler et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction citing Monti, 2010 for arousal.

evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction citing multiple sources.

claim: Serotonergic signaling pathways are targets of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs).
source: Serotonergic signaling pathways are also targets of widely-used therapeutic drugs, such as selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) and atypical antipsychotics (Meltzer and Massey, 2011; Vaswani et al., 2003).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction citing Meltzer and Massey, 2011 and Vaswani et al., 2003.

claim: Many serotonergic drugs can acutely induce adverse side effects including anxiety and increased risk of suicidal behaviors.
source: However many of these drugs can acutely induce adverse side effects including anxiety and increased risk of suicidal behaviors (Ferguson, 2001; Gartlehner et al., 2011; Vaswani et al., 2003).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction citing Ferguson, 2001, Gartlehner et al., 2011, and Vaswani et al., 2003.

claim: Only 30% to 50% of neurons in the DRN are serotonergic.
source: Neurons in the DRN are neurochemically and anatomically diverse – only 30% to 50% are serotonergic, and many release other neurotransmitters including GABA, glutamate, dopamine (DA), nitric oxide, and a variety of peptides (Fu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction citing Fu et al., 2010.

claim: Many DRN neurons release neurotransmitters including GABA, glutamate, dopamine, nitric oxide, and a variety of peptides.
source: Neurons in the DRN are neurochemically and anatomically diverse – only 30% to 50% are serotonergic, and many release other neurotransmitters including GABA, glutamate, dopamine (DA), nitric oxide, and a variety of peptides (Fu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction citing Fu et al., 2010.

claim: Some DRN neurons co-express genes that are traditionally used as markers for different neuronal cell types based on their neurotransmitter usage.
source: Some DRN neurons co-express genes that are traditionally used as markers for different neuronal cell types based on their neurotransmitter usage (e.g. Gad1, Gad2, Slc17a6, and Slc17a8) (Fu et al., 2010; Okaty et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction citing Fu et al., 2010 and Okaty et al., 2015.

claim: The DRN contains the 5-HT neuron clusters B6 and B7.
source: Cytoarchitecturally, the DRN contains the 5-HT neuron clusters B6 and B7 (Dahlström and Fuxe, 1964; Hornung, 2010), and is further divided into subregions along all three major anatomical axes (Hale and Lowry, 2011).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction citing Dahlström and Fuxe, 1964 and Hornung, 2010.

claim: The DRN is further divided into subregions along all three major anatomical axes.
source: Cytoarchitecturally, the DRN contains the 5-HT neuron clusters B6 and B7 (Dahlström and Fuxe, 1964; Hornung, 2010), and is further divided into subregions along all three major anatomical axes (Hale and Lowry, 2011).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction citing Hale and Lowry, 2011.

claim: DRN 5-HT neurons share a common developmental lineage.
source: Although DRN 5-HT neurons share a common developmental lineage (Deneris and Gaspar, 2018; Jensen et al., 2008), DRN 5-HT neurons in different subregions express different G protein-coupled receptors and vesicular transporters, suggesting spatial clustering of functionally specialized neurons (Calizo et al., 2011; Fernandez et al., 2016; Lowry et al., 2000; Templin et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction citing Deneris and Gaspar, 2018 and Jensen et al., 2008.

claim: DRN 5-HT neurons in different subregions express different G protein-coupled receptors and vesicular transporters.
source: Although DRN 5-HT neurons share a common developmental lineage (Deneris and Gaspar, 2018; Jensen et al., 2008), DRN 5-HT neurons in different subregions express different G protein-coupled receptors and vesicular transporters, suggesting spatial clustering of functionally specialized neurons (Calizo et al., 2011; Fernandez et al., 2016; Lowry et al., 2000; Templin et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction citing multiple sources.

claim: Individual 5-HT neurons have extensive collateralization of axons.
source: This likely arises, in part, from the extensive collateralization of axons from individual 5-HT neurons (Gagnon and Parent, 2014; Waselus et al., 2011) – different 5-HT neurons are therefore likely to have overlapping axonal projection fields, even if they target distinct sets of regions to serve separate functions.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction citing Gagnon and Parent, 2014 and Waselus et al., 2011.

claim: Functional differences exist between projection-defined subpopulations of DRN 5-HT neurons.
source: Functional differences exist between projection-defined subpopulations of DRN 5-HT neurons (Ren et al., 2018), but it is unknown if these subpopulations map onto molecularly defined subtypes.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the introduction citing Ren et al., 2018.

claim: The processed dataset contained 39,411 cells from eight mice (4 male and 4 female, age range 8–10 weeks).
source: The processed dataset contained 39,411 cells from eight mice (4 male and 4 female, age range 8–10 weeks) with a median UMIFM count of 2,333 counts per cell (min. = 548; max. = 17,976; IQR = 1,903) and median gene detection rate of 1,034 genes per cell (min. = 216; max. = 5,765; IQR = 693).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section describing the dataset.

evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section describing the dataset.

claim: Cells from male and female mice were pooled for analysis as no major transcriptional sex differences were observed.
source: Cells from male and female mice were pooled for analysis as no major transcriptional sex differences were observed (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Transcripts encoding 8 of the 15 5-HT receptors in the mouse genome were detected in the dataset.
source: Transcripts encoding 8 of the 15 5-HT receptors in the mouse genome were detected in our dataset (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section with reference to Figure 2A.

claim: Htr1a, Htr1b, Htr2c, Htr5b, and Htr7 were strongly expressed in different subsets of cells.
source: Of these Htr1a, Htr1b, Htr2c, Htr5b, and Htr7 were strongly expressed in different subsets of cells.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section describing gene expression patterns.

claim: The autoinhibitory Gi-coupled receptor Htr1a was expressed primarily in 5-HT neurons.
source: The autoinhibitory Gi-coupled receptor Htr1a was expressed primarily in 5-HT neurons, whereas the Gq-coupled Htr2c receptor was expressed in both GABAergic and glutamatergic neurons (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section with reference to Figure 2B.

claim: The Gq-coupled Htr2c receptor was expressed in both GABAergic and glutamatergic neurons.
source: The autoinhibitory Gi-coupled receptor Htr1a was expressed primarily in 5-HT neurons, whereas the Gq-coupled Htr2c receptor was expressed in both GABAergic and glutamatergic neurons (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section with reference to Figure 2B.

claim: The Gi-coupled Htr1b receptor is expressed in both 5-HT neurons and pvMΦs of the DRN.
source: Additionally, we unexpectedly observed expression of the Gi-coupled Htr1b receptor in both 5-HT neurons and pvMΦs of the DRN (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section with reference to Figure 2C.

claim: Expression of Htr1b in pvMΦs is unique to the DRN and its close surroundings.
source: Examination of Htr1b expression in cortex, striatum, and ventral midbrain suggests that expression of this receptor in pvMΦs is unique to the DRN and its close surroundings (Hrvatin et al., 2018; Saunders et al., 2018; Zeisel et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section citing multiple sources.

claim: Htr5b was found in ependymal cells and a subset of 5-HT neurons.
source: Htr5b, which is a pseudogene in humans (Grailhe et al., 2001), was found in ependymal cells and a subset of 5-HT neurons.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section citing Grailhe et al., 2001.

claim: The Gs-coupled Htr7 receptor was found in a small subset of GABAergic and glutamatergic neurons.
source: The Gs-coupled Htr7 receptor was also found in a small subset of GABAergic and glutamatergic neurons.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section describing gene expression patterns.

claim: Subclustering conservatively separated the 2,041 neurons into 18 distinct clusters.
source: Subclustering conservatively separated the 2,041 neurons into 18 distinct clusters, which we aggregated into 5 major groups based on similarities in their expression of genes, most notably those involved in the synthesis and release of different neurotransmitters (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section with reference to Figure 3A.

claim: The 18 neuronal clusters were aggregated into 5 major groups based on similarities in their expression of genes involved in the synthesis and release of different neurotransmitters.
source: Subclustering conservatively separated the 2,041 neurons into 18 distinct clusters, which we aggregated into 5 major groups based on similarities in their expression of genes, most notably those involved in the synthesis and release of different neurotransmitters (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section with reference to Figure 3A.

claim: Gad1 and Gad2 are expressed in GABAergic neurons and a subset of both 5-HT and glutamatergic DRN neurons.
source: These genes included Gad1 and Gad2, which encode GABA synthetic enzymes and are expressed in GABAergic neurons and a subset of both 5-HT and glutamatergic DRN neurons, as well as Slc17a6, which encodes a vesicular glutamate transporter and is expressed in most DRN glutamatergic and DA neurons.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section describing gene expression patterns.

claim: Slc17a6 is expressed in most DRN glutamatergic and DA neurons.
source: These genes included Gad1 and Gad2, which encode GABA synthetic enzymes and are expressed in GABAergic neurons and a subset of both 5-HT and glutamatergic DRN neurons, as well as Slc17a6, which encodes a vesicular glutamate transporter and is expressed in most DRN glutamatergic and DA neurons.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section describing gene expression patterns.

claim: Cells co-expressing Slc32a1, Slc17a6, and Crhbp were found in anterior regions of the DRN in the caudal linear nucleus (CLi) and dorsomedial DRN.
source: Cells expressing Slc32a1, Slc17a6, and Crhbp were found in anterior regions of the DRN in the caudal linear nucleus (CLi) and dorsomedial DRN in close proximity to the cerebral aqueduct.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section describing the location of cells expressing specific genes.

claim: The GABA/Glu cluster represents 0.08% (32 of 39,411) of cells in the scRNA-seq dataset.
source: Thus, this cluster, representing just 0.08% (32 of 39,411) of cells in the scRNA-seq dataset, corresponds to a bona fide and previously unrecognized neuronal cell type within the DRN that may be a caudal extension of the recently described GABA/Glu neuron group of the ventral midbrain (Root et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section citing Root et al., 2018.

claim: DRN 5-HT neurons separated into five distinct subtypes.
source: DRN 5-HT neurons (n = 704 cells) separated into five distinct subtypes.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section describing the clustering of 5-HT neurons.

claim: 333 differentially expressed genes were found between 5-HT neuron subtypes at a 5% false discovery rate.
source: We found 333 differentially expressed genes (DE genes) by performing differential expression tests at each node on the cluster dendrogram at a 5% false discovery rate (Benjamini-Hochberg correction).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section describing the differential expression analysis.

claim: Genes involved in neuronal development and identity specification were overrepresented in the transcripts differentiating the 5-HT subtypes.
source: Enrichment tests for gene ontology (GO) terms and analysis of DE genes with annotated functions showed that genes involved in neuronal development and identity specification, such as transcription factors, and genes involved in specifying neuronal connectivity, such as cell adhesion and axon guidance molecules, were overrepresented in the transcripts differentiating the 5-HT subtypes (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Genes involved in specifying neuronal connectivity were overrepresented in the transcripts differentiating the 5-HT subtypes.
source: Enrichment tests for gene ontology (GO) terms and analysis of DE genes with annotated functions showed that genes involved in neuronal development and identity specification, such as transcription factors, and genes involved in specifying neuronal connectivity, such as cell adhesion and axon guidance molecules, were overrepresented in the transcripts differentiating the 5-HT subtypes (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: 193 of 333 DE genes encoded for membrane proteins.
source: A large proportion of DE genes encoded for membrane proteins (GO:0016020 – membrane, 193 of 333 DE genes) with functions in neurotransmission and regulating intrinsic cellular excitability, such as neurotransmitter receptors, ion channels, vesicular transporters, neuropeptides, and other proteins involved in the synthesis or reuptake of neurotransmitters (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section with reference to Figure 4A.

claim: The 5-HT-V subtype was the most transcriptionally distinct.
source: The cluster dendrogram for 5-HT neuron subtypes showed that the smallest subtype cluster 5-HT-V (n = 7 cells) was the most transcriptionally distinct, was marked by expression of genes such as Met, P2ry1, and Trpc3 (Figure 4—figure supplement 3C), and lacked expression of genes for GABA co-transmission.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 3C.

claim: 5-HT-V subtype neurons are located in the posterior B6 tail of the DRN.
source: Inspection of ISHs probing these genes suggests that 5-HT-V subtype neurons are located in the posterior B6 tail of the DRN (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section with reference to Figure 4B.

claim: Subtypes 5-HT-I and 5-HT-II had enriched expression of genes for GABAergic neurotransmission such as Gad1 and Slc6a1.
source: The remaining four subtypes separated into two groups: the first was comprised of subtypes 5-HT-I (n = 178 cells) and 5-HT-II (n = 186 cells) that had enriched expression of genes for GABAergic neurotransmission such as Gad1 and Slc6a1, and the calcium-independent protein kinase Prkcq.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section describing gene expression patterns.

claim: Subtypes 5-HT-III and 5-HT-IV were enriched in genes such as Adcy2.
source: The second group was comprised of subtypes 5-HT-III (n = 125 cells) and 5-HT-IV (n = 208 cells) that were enriched in genes such as Adcy2, which was not expressed in the 5-HT-I/II group.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section describing gene expression patterns.

claim: Genes enriched in subtypes 5-HT-I and 5-HT-II were expressed in lateral parts of the DRN.
source: Genes enriched in subtypes 5-HT-I and 5-HT-II were expressed in lateral parts of the DRN (Figure 4C–D), whereas genes enriched in subtypes 5-HT-III and 5-HT-IV showed enrichment in medial parts of the DRN along the midline (Figure 4E–F).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section with reference to Figures 4C-D.

claim: Genes enriched in subtypes 5-HT-III and 5-HT-IV showed enrichment in medial parts of the DRN along the midline.
source: Genes enriched in subtypes 5-HT-I and 5-HT-II were expressed in lateral parts of the DRN (Figure 4C–D), whereas genes enriched in subtypes 5-HT-III and 5-HT-IV showed enrichment in medial parts of the DRN along the midline (Figure 4E–F).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section with reference to Figures 4E-F.

claim: Correlation coefficients between the normalized expression scores for 112 DE genes for each voxel and each 5-HT neuron subtype cluster were calculated.
source: Subsequently, correlation coefficients between the normalized expression scores for 112 DE genes for each of these voxels and each 5-HT neuron subtype cluster were calculated (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D, Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 1D and Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Subtype 5-HT-V showed a tight distribution within the dorsomedial posterior B6 tail of the DRN.
source: Most subtypes were not confined to a specific DRN subregion, with the exception of subtype 5-HT-V (Figure 5, purple) that showed a tight distribution within the dorsomedial posterior B6 tail of the DRN.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section with reference to Figure 5.

claim: Subtypes 5-HT-I and 5-HT-II occupied the dorsolateral subregions in the posterior half of the DRN where they are likely spatially intermingled.
source: Subtypes 5-HT-I and 5-HT-II showed the greatest similarities in spatial distribution – both subtypes occupied the dorsolateral subregions in the posterior half of the DRN where they are likely spatially intermingled, consistent with their higher expression of GABAergic transmission genes Gad1 and Gad2.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section describing the spatial distribution of subtypes.

claim: Subtype 5-HT-III showed the highest correlations with voxels in the dorsomedial part of the DRN in its anterior half.
source: This overlaps with the distribution of the Pdyn-enriched subtype 5-HT-III (Figure 5, green), which showed the highest correlations with voxels in the dorsomedial part of the DRN in its anterior half.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section with reference to Figure 5.

claim: Subtype 5-HT-IV occupied most of the ventral DRN.
source: Both subtypes 5-HT-III and 5-HT-IV (Figure 5, blue) showed higher correlations with voxels along the midline, but were separated along the dorsal-ventral axis with the Slc17a8-enriched 5-HT-IV subtype occupying most of the ventral DRN.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section with reference to Figure 5.

claim: Approximately one-third of all DRN 5-HT neurons innervate the striatum.
source: The nuclei of the basal ganglia are major targets of DRN 5-HT neurons, with approximately one-third of all DRN 5-HT neurons innervating the striatum (Str) (Steinbusch et al., 1981).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section citing Steinbusch et al., 1981.

claim: Most projection-defined subpopulations were located either ipsilateral to the injection site or along the midline.
source: Most projection-defined subpopulations were located either ipsilateral to the injection site or along the midline, with the exception of the habenula-projecting neurons which were found in both ipsilateral and contralateral lateral wings of the DRN (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section with reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Most subcortical-projecting neurons were located in the dorsal DRN.
source: Consistent with previous reports (Ren et al., 2018; Waterhouse et al., 1986), we found that most subcortical-projecting neurons were located in the dorsal DRN, whereas most cortical-projecting neurons were located in the ventral DRN.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section citing Ren et al., 2018 and Waterhouse et al., 1986.

claim: Most cortical-projecting neurons were located in the ventral DRN.
source: Consistent with previous reports (Ren et al., 2018; Waterhouse et al., 1986), we found that most subcortical-projecting neurons were located in the dorsal DRN, whereas most cortical-projecting neurons were located in the ventral DRN.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section citing Ren et al., 2018 and Waterhouse et al., 1986.

claim: DRN neurons innervating both Str and M1 were often found in the ventrolateral DRN and dorsal border of the ventromedial DRN.
source: Double retrograde tracing experiments also showed that DRN neurons innervating both Str and M1 were often found in these regions (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section with reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Cortical-projecting subpopulations of DRN 5-HT neurons express Slc17a8.
source: It has been reported that cortical-projecting subpopulations of DRN 5-HT neurons express Slc17a8, in agreement with the extensive overlap between the spatial distribution of cortical-projecting neurons and Slc17a8 expression (Ren et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section citing Ren et al., 2018.

claim: 52% of Str-projecting DRN 5-HT neurons expressed Pdyn.
source: We found that Str-projecting DRN 5-HT neurons expressed the subtype 5-HT-III enriched gene Pdyn (52%, 39 of 75 RbV-labeled 5-HT neurons) or the 5-HT-IV enriched gene Cbln2 (46%, 49 of 106 RbV-labeled 5-HT neurons), consistent with the overlap in the distribution of this projection-defined subpopulation with the inferred distributions of these two distinct subtypes.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section reporting quantification of gene expression in projection-defined neurons.

claim: 46% of Str-projecting DRN 5-HT neurons expressed Cbln2.
source: We found that Str-projecting DRN 5-HT neurons expressed the subtype 5-HT-III enriched gene Pdyn (52%, 39 of 75 RbV-labeled 5-HT neurons) or the 5-HT-IV enriched gene Cbln2 (46%, 49 of 106 RbV-labeled 5-HT neurons), consistent with the overlap in the distribution of this projection-defined subpopulation with the inferred distributions of these two distinct subtypes.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section reporting quantification of gene expression in projection-defined neurons.

claim: 57% of Str-projecting DRN 5-HT neurons expressed Slc17a8.
source: A subset of Str-projecting neurons also expressed Slc17a8 (57%, 70 of 123 RbV-labeled 5-HT neurons), which is enriched in 5-HT-IV but also expressed in 5-HT-III at lower levels.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section reporting quantification of gene expression in projection-defined neurons.

claim: 4% of Str-projecting DRN 5-HT neurons expressed Trh.
source: Few Str-projecting neurons expressed Trh (4%, 4 of 102 RbV-labeled 5-HT neurons).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section reporting quantification of gene expression in projection-defined neurons.

claim: The Str-projecting DRN 5-HT neuron subpopulation is molecularly heterogeneous and is comprised of at least 2 transcriptionally distinct 5-HT neuron subtypes.
source: Therefore, our results support the hypothesis that the Str-projecting DRN 5-HT neuron subpopulation is molecularly heterogeneous, and is comprised of at least 2 transcriptionally distinct 5-HT neuron subtypes.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section summarizing findings about the Str-projecting subpopulation.

claim: mCitrine-labeled axons from Pdyn+;Pet1+ neurons were found in a subset of regions innervated by DRN Pet1+ neurons.
source: mCitrine-labeled axons from Pdyn+;Pet1+ neurons were found in a subset of regions innervated by DRN Pet1+ neurons (Figure 8B–F, Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section with reference to Figure 8B–F and Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: The output nuclei of the basal ganglia, including the ventral pallidum (VP), entopeduncular nucleus (EP), and substantia nigra pars reticulata (SNr), were most densely innervated by Pdyn+;Pet1+ neurons.
source: Of the regions innervated by both DRN Pet1+ neurons and Pdyn+;Pet1+ neurons, the output nuclei of the basal ganglia, including the ventral pallidum (VP), entopeduncular nucleus (EP), and substantia nigra pars reticulata (SNr), were most densely innervated by Pdyn+;Pet1+ neurons (Figure 8B–D).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section with reference to Figure 8B–D.

claim: Sensory structures, such as the dLGN, were not innervated by Pdyn+;Pet1+ neurons.
source: In contrast, sensory structures, such as the dLGN (Figure 8E), and limbic structures, such as the hypothalamus (Figure 8F) were not innervated by Pdyn+;Pet1+ neurons, despite receiving dense input from DRN Pet1+ neurons.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section with reference to Figure 8E.

claim: Limbic structures, such as the hypothalamus, were not innervated by Pdyn+;Pet1+ neurons.
source: In contrast, sensory structures, such as the dLGN (Figure 8E), and limbic structures, such as the hypothalamus (Figure 8F) were not innervated by Pdyn+;Pet1+ neurons, despite receiving dense input from DRN Pet1+ neurons.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section with reference to Figure 8F.

claim: The Pdyn+ subtype 5-HT-III neurons broadly but selectively innervate structures that are either a part of or functionally linked to the basal ganglia.
source: These results therefore demonstrate that the Pdyn+ subtype 5-HT-III neurons broadly but selectively innervate structures that are either a part of or functionally linked to the basal ganglia, and are unlikely to be involved in sensory modulation.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section summarizing findings about the Pdyn+ subtype.

claim: The Pdyn+ subtype 5-HT-III neurons are unlikely to be involved in sensory modulation.
source: These results therefore demonstrate that the Pdyn+ subtype 5-HT-III neurons broadly but selectively innervate structures that are either a part of or functionally linked to the basal ganglia, and are unlikely to be involved in sensory modulation.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the results section summarizing findings about the Pdyn+ subtype.

claim: The study uncovered 5 subtypes of DRN 5-HT neurons based on their gene expression profiles.
source: We uncovered 5 subtypes of DRN 5-HT neurons based on their gene expression profiles and showed that these are organized into distinct spatial domains within the DRN that are segregated along all three major anatomical axes.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the discussion summarizing the main findings.

claim: The 5 subtypes of DRN 5-HT neurons are organized into distinct spatial domains within the DRN that are segregated along all three major anatomical axes.
source: We uncovered 5 subtypes of DRN 5-HT neurons based on their gene expression profiles and showed that these are organized into distinct spatial domains within the DRN that are segregated along all three major anatomical axes.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the discussion summarizing the main findings.

claim: The spatial organization of molecularly defined 5-HT neurons does not conform to anatomical subdivisions as defined by cytoarchitecture of the DRN or the projection targets of 5-HT axons.
source: However, the spatial organization of molecularly defined 5-HT neurons does not conform to anatomical subdivisions as defined by cytoarchitecture of the DRN or the projection targets of 5-HT axons.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the discussion summarizing the main findings.

claim: The study defines a Pdyn-enriched 5-HT neuron subtype that is well-positioned to broadly but specifically alter the input and output of basal ganglia circuits.
source: We also define a Pdyn-enriched 5-HT neuron subtype that is well-positioned to broadly but specifically alter the input and output of basal ganglia circuits, potentially mediating the modulation of motor control, decision making, and reinforcement learning by internal state.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the discussion summarizing the main findings.

claim: Each cytoarchitecturally-defined DRN subregion contains different molecularly-defined 5-HT subtypes.
source: We reconstructed the spatial distribution of each 5-HT subtype using spatial correlation analysis of gene differentially expressed between subtypes and showed that each cytoarchitecturally-defined DRN subregion contains different molecularly-defined 5-HT subtypes.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the discussion summarizing the main findings.

claim: The B6 5-HT neuron cluster is transcriptionally more similar to 5-HT neurons in the median raphe nucleus.
source: Previous reports have suggested that the B6 5-HT neuron cluster is transcriptionally more similar to 5-HT neurons in the median raphe nucleus, despite being a part of the cytoarchitecturally-defined DRN (Commons, 2015).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the discussion citing Commons, 2015.

claim: The 5-HT-IV subtype neurons were distributed throughout most of the anterior-posterior extent of the ventral DRN.
source: We noted that 5-HT-IV neurons were distributed throughout most of the anterior-posterior extent of the ventral DRN, although it is suggested that there is a topographical organization of cortical projecting 5-HT neurons along this axis.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the discussion describing the spatial distribution of the 5-HT-IV subtype.

claim: The dorsolateral DRN showed strongly negative correlations with the 5-HT-IV subtype.
source: In comparison, the dorsolateral DRN, also called the lateral wings of the DRN (lwDRN) and ventrolateral DRN (DRVL), showed strongly negative correlations with the 5-HT-IV subtype, particularly in the posterior half of the DRN where there is clearer spatial separation of Tph2+ neurons into medial and lateral compartments.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the discussion describing the spatial distribution of subtypes.

claim: Subtypes 5-HT-I and 5-HT-II were intermingled in the dorsolateral subregion.
source: Subtypes 5-HT-I and 5-HT-II were intermingled in this region, which is enriched in Trh, a 5-HT-I enriched gene.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the discussion describing the spatial distribution of subtypes.

claim: The dorsolateral subregion innervates many subcortical sensory and hypothalamic nuclei, in addition to motor nuclei in the brainstem.
source: The dorsolateral subregion innervates many subcortical sensory and hypothalamic nuclei, in addition to motor nuclei in the brainstem (Lee et al., 2008; Muzerelle et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the discussion citing Lee et al., 2008 and Muzerelle et al., 2016.

claim: The close spatial proximity of subtypes 5-HT-I and 5-HT-II presents a plausible mechanism for competitive inhibition between these separate subsystems via 5-HT1A receptors and local 5-HT release.
source: Additionally, the close spatial proximity of these two subtypes also presents a plausible mechanism for competitive inhibition between these separate subsystems via 5-HT1A receptors and local 5-HT release, which may be relevant to selective sensory modulation by movement or changes in behavioral state (Hall et al., 2010; Yokogawa et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the discussion citing Hall et al., 2010 and Yokogawa et al., 2012.

claim: Subtype distributions are not confined within cytoarchitecturally-defined subregion boundaries, especially in the anterior half of the DRN.
source: Furthermore, a detailed comparison of the 5-HT subtype distributions with cytoarchitecturally-defined subregion boundaries showed that subtype distributions are not confined within these subregion boundaries, especially in the anterior half of the DRN.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the discussion describing the spatial distribution of subtypes.

claim: The poor correspondence between molecularly-inferred and cytoarchitecturally-defined spatial domains cautions against the use of anatomical subregions for targeting 5-HT subsystems.
source: The poor correspondence between molecularly-inferred and cytoarchitecturally-defined spatial domains cautions against the use of anatomical subregions for targeting 5-HT subsystems.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the discussion summarizing implications of the findings.

claim: Many of the physiological and anatomical differences between 5-HT neuron subtypes are a result of molecular differences specified by expression of overlapping but distinct transcriptional networks.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, our results suggest that many of the physiological and anatomical differences between 5-HT neuron subtypes are a result of molecular differences specified by expression of overlapping but distinct transcriptional networks.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the discussion summarizing implications of the findings.

claim: The study does not seek to present a definitive catalogue of all neuron subtypes present in the DRN.
source: Thus our study does not seek to present a definitive catalogue of all neuron subtypes present in the DRN, since the techniques used are limited in their ability to resolve finer levels of heterogeneity and differential expression of low copy transcripts.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the discussion acknowledging limitations of the study.

claim: Histaminergic paracrine signaling from ependymal cells can exert differential effects on various neuronal subtypes based on proximity to the cerebral aqueduct and differential expression of histaminergic receptors.
source: Histaminergic paracrine signaling from ependymal cells can exert differential effects on various neuronal subtypes based on proximity to the cerebral aqueduct and differential expression of histaminergic receptors.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the discussion describing potential local interactions.

claim: The histamine receptors Hrh1 and Hrh3 are expressed in 5-HT subtypes 5-HT-I, 5-HT-II, and 5-HT-III.
source: Notably, the histamine receptors Hrh1 and Hrh3 are expressed in 5-HT subtypes 5-HT-I, 5-HT-II, and 5-HT-III, which are all located in dorsal DRN subregions in close proximity to the cerebral aqueduct.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the discussion describing gene expression patterns.

claim: 5-HT-IV subtype neurons do not express detectable levels of Hrh1 and express Hrh3 at very low levels.
source: In contrast, 5-HT-IV subtype neurons, which are in ventral subregions further from the aqueduct, do not express detectable levels of Hrh1 and express Hrh3 at very low levels.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the discussion describing gene expression patterns.

claim: Expression of the Gi-coupled Htr1b receptor on pvMΦs within or in close proximity to the DRN is unique compared to pvMΦs in brain regions that do not contain 5-HT neurons.
source: We also found that pvMΦs within or in close proximity to the DRN express the Gi-coupled Htr1b receptor, unlike pvMΦs in brain regions that do not contain 5-HT neurons.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the discussion describing gene expression patterns.

claim: Activation of Gi-coupled pathways on pvMΦs via 5-HT1B receptors is a potential mechanism for the regulation of macrophage polarization and inflammatory responses by tonic 5-HT release within the DRN.
source: Activation of Gi-coupled pathways on pvMΦs via 5-HT1B receptors is also a potential mechanism for the regulation of macrophage polarization and inflammatory responses by tonic 5-HT release within the DRN, which may be relevant to the increasing importance of neuroinflammatory pathways in the etiology of psychiatric disorders (Brisch et al., 2017; Howerton et al., 2014; Watkins et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the discussion citing Brisch et al., 2017, Howerton et al., 2014, and Watkins et al., 2014.

claim: Somatodendritic release of 5-HT and activation of inhibitory 5-HT1A receptors on adjacent 5-HT neurons is likely to mediate lateral inhibition between the 5-HT neurons of the same subtype.
source: For direct signaling between 5-HT neurons, somatodendritic release of 5-HT and activation of inhibitory 5-HT1A receptors on adjacent 5-HT neurons is likely to mediate lateral inhibition between the 5-HT neurons of the same subtype, due to the spatial clustering of the subtypes.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the discussion describing potential local interactions.

claim: The subsystem comprised of the Pdyn-enriched subtype 5-HT-III sends broad projections to both input and output nuclei of the basal ganglia.
source: We showed that the subsystem comprised of the Pdyn-enriched subtype 5-HT-III sends broad projections to both input and output nuclei of the basal ganglia, while avoiding other sensory and limbic structures, which have distinct functions from the basal ganglia and are likely to receive inputs from other DRN 5-HT neuron subtypes.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the discussion summarizing findings about the Pdyn-enriched subtype.

claim: The dense innervation of basal ganglia output nuclei by 5-HT-III neurons suggests that this 5-HT subsystem has a prominent role in the regulation of motor output and action selection.
source: Although we also showed that the basal ganglia receives inputs from multiple 5-HT neuron subtypes, particularly in the case of the Str-projecting subpopulation, the dense innervation of basal ganglia output nuclei by 5-HT-III neurons suggests that this 5-HT subsystem has a prominent role in the regulation of motor output and action selection through its effects on the activity of basal ganglia output nuclei.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the discussion summarizing implications of the findings.

claim: 5-HT release from the Pdyn-enriched subsystem may have different effects on distinct output channels of the basal ganglia.
source: We also speculate that 5-HT release from this subsystem may have different effects on distinct output channels of the basal ganglia, given the differential expression of 5-HT receptors on distinct subpopulations of SNr and EP projection neurons (Saunders et al., 2018; Wallace et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the discussion citing Saunders et al., 2018 and Wallace et al., 2017.
